title: One tree or many?
description: Course activity for Exercise 6: compare a single regression tree, bagging, and a Random Forest across five deterministic training replicates for predicting age from brain structure.
instructions: Choose a number of trees, then pick which model to highlight in the prediction panel. The top panel shows each model's validation MSE across all five training replicates; the middle panel shows how validation MSE changes as more trees are added to bagging and the Random Forest; the bottom panel shows observed-versus-predicted age, using one fixed training sample, for the model you selected.
randomForestNote: Random Forest combines bootstrap sampling with a random subset of features considered at each split. Bagging uses every feature at every split; only the training sample changes from tree to tree.
reflectionPrompts: Which model changed the most as you switched between training replicates?
Did adding more trees change the average validation MSE, its variability across replicates, or both?
At roughly how many trees do bagging and Random Forest results start to stabilize?
Did the Random Forest outperform bagging at every number of trees, or only some?
Why does averaging many trees reduce variance without making any individual tree shallower?
